YOUR AFTERNOON COFFEE MIGHT BE CONTRIBUTING TO THE SLEEP PROBLEM YOU’RE TRYING TO FIX You’re exhausted by lunchtime, so what do you do? Reach for another cup of coffee. It gives you a temporary boost, but when bedtime comes, you find yourself struggling to fall asleep. Caffeine blocks adenosine, a chemical that helps build sleep pressure throughout the day. Because caffeine can remain in your system for several hours, that afternoon coffee may interfere with your ability to fall asleep and maintain quality sleep.” Experiment with moving your caffeine cutoff earlier in the day. Try avoiding caffeine at least six to eight hours before bedtime, and see how your sleep responds. You may discover that you don’t need another coffee; you need better rest! FOLLOW FOR MORE NATURAL WAYS YO RESTORE HEALTH. #menopause  #WomenOver50  #poorsleep #coffeandsleep #sleeppressure
